label: X-01
evidence: crates/sealmap-model/src/source.rs:163-167 filter_entry skips skip_dirs (target, node_modules, vendor, dist, build, out; :64) at any depth>0; :177-179 continue when len > max_file_bytes (2 MiB default, :65); :181 continue on non-UTF-8; :182 continue on relativisation failure; no diagnostic emitted. crates/sealmap-rust/src/lib.rs:182-184 and crates/sealmap/src/lib.rs:115-118 use these defaults. Contract text at crates/sealmap-corpus/src/lib.rs:9-10; parse-failure placeholder at crates/sealmap-rust/src/collect.rs:57-59 and diagnostics at resolve.rs:217-221 exist only for files that loaded.
rationale: Load-time drops really are silent and nothing in the outputs records them, while parse failures are surfaced, so a src/build/ directory or an oversized or non-UTF-8 .rs file vanishes without notice. LoadOptions documents the filters, but the CLI has no way to see or report what was dropped.

label: X-02
evidence: crates/sealmap/src/lib.rs:100-126 prefixes only file paths with the repo name; crates/sealmap-rust/src/layout.rs:46-59 takes the crate identity from [package] name alone; crates/sealmap-model/src/codebase.rs:66-87 add_symbol merges same-id symbols silently; crates/sealmap-corpus/src/naming.rs:23-30 only panics when distinct ids collide. Reproduced with a temporary test: two repos api/common and core/common, each with `pub struct A` plus a different method, produced one `sym:cargo common . A#` carrying both `A#fa().` and `A#fc().`, with two documents emitted.
rationale: Crates with the same name in different repos collapse into one set of symbol ids, so the repos' symbols merge with no warning, which contradicts the generate_repos documentation.

label: X-03
evidence: crates/sealmap/src/main.rs:158-161 sets ro.name = dir_name(&c.path) when no --name is given, and dir_name (:177-182) uses the canonicalised directory's file_name. The name reaches output at crates/sealmap-corpus/src/index.rs:105 (_index.json codebase) and overview.rs:17,21. Determinism claims at crates/sealmap/src/lib.rs:64-66 and corpus_hash at contract.rs:172-183; CI pins --name at .github/workflows/ci.yml:25.
rationale: Two clones of the same commit in differently named directories produce different bytes in _index.json and _overview.md. That breaks the 'same sources on any machine' promise unless every caller pins --name.

label: X-04
evidence: crates/sealmap-extract/src/isolate.rs:8-10,29,45-48 uses catch_unwind and a 64 MiB stack, and its own doc says a stack overflow cannot be caught. crates/sealmap-rust/src/collect.rs:30 MAX_EXPR_DEPTH bounds only the expression walker (:1078-1083), not syn's parse. Reproduced: a 1.6 MB src/lib.rs (under the 2 MiB cap) containing `pub type T = Option<` nested 200000 levels made the release `sealmap model` binary abort with 'has overflowed its stack', exit 134, no diagnostic.
rationale: One deeply nested file under the size cap kills the whole run, and the panic isolation cannot catch it. The code documents this, but it remains a real, deterministic denial-of-service path.
